Appearance:
 Shri Akhil Singh - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Atmaram Ben - Dy.G.A. for the respondent/State.
 None for the victim, despite service of notice.

Order 
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail in relation to FIR No.21/2024, dated 31.01.2024 registered at Police Station-Dehat, District - Maihar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 363,
366-A, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 17.08.2024.
2 As per the prosecution story, on 31.01.2024, father of 17 years and 6 months old prosecutrix lodged FIR about missing of his daughter since 10:00 A.M. of 29.01.2024.
FIR was registered.
In the course of investigation, prosecutrix was recovered and she in her statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS
stated that she was having love relations with Raja and she has entered into wedlock with him and now carrying 5 months pregnancy.
3 Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is 23 years old boy who was having love affair with the prosecutrix.
They have consensually established physical relations with each other and as a result of their NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50779 2 MCRC-42952-2024 relationship prosecutrix has become pregnant.
They are husband and wife.
Therefore, no offence of rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault is made out against the applicant.
Hence, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.

5 Considering the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 183 of BNSS and other facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 It is directed that applicant - Raja Bhaiya be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS/437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50779 3 MCRC-42952-2024 Jasleen Raja Bhaiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81642866/
